examBlueprint.tests: B8.1: the phylogenetic tree built from shared characters
Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B8.2 (the natural-selection passage)

standards.title: Descent with modification
standards.description: Students explain Darwin's core idea and the evidence for common ancestry.
iCan: I can state Darwin's idea of descent with modification: living species descended, with changes, from common ancestors
I can read a phylogenetic tree as a hypothesis of shared ancestry, where each branch point is a common ancestor
I can describe the evidence for common ancestry: the fossil record, homologous structures, vestigial structures, molecular and DNA similarity, and biogeography
I can tell the difference between homology (shared ancestry) and analogy (similar function, independent origin)

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q2, Q3; SA 11, 12; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Natural selection
standards.description: Students explain how natural selection produces adaptation.
iCan: I can state the conditions for natural selection: heritable variation, more offspring than can survive, and some variants survive and reproduce better
I can explain that individuals with favorable heritable traits leave more offspring, so those traits become more common over generations
I can define adaptation and fitness, and explain that the population evolves, not the individual
I can correct common misconceptions: individuals do not evolve in a lifetime, and traits are not acquired by need or use

exam.examItems: MC Q4, Q5, Q6; SA 13, 14; Part 3 CER

standards.title: Hardy-Weinberg and genetic variation
standards.description: Students use allele frequencies to define and detect evolution.
iCan: I can define a gene pool and allele frequency, and define evolution as a change in allele frequencies over generations
I can state the Hardy-Weinberg equations (p + q = 1 and p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1) and say what each term means
I can list the five conditions for equilibrium and explain that equilibrium means no evolution
I can use the equations to calculate allele and genotype frequencies from data

standards.title: Mechanisms of evolution
standards.description: Students compare the processes that change allele frequencies.
iCan: I can explain that natural selection is the only mechanism that consistently produces adaptation
I can explain genetic drift (random change, strong in small populations) and the bottleneck and founder effects
I can explain gene flow (alleles moving between populations) and that it tends to reduce differences
I can name mutation as the source of new alleles, and tell apart directional, stabilizing, and disruptive selection

standards.title: Speciation
standards.description: Students explain how one species becomes two.
iCan: I can state the biological species concept (members can interbreed and produce fertile offspring; different species cannot)
I can tell prezygotic barriers (prevent mating or fertilization) from postzygotic barriers (hybrids inviable or sterile)
I can tell allopatric speciation (a geographic barrier separates populations) from sympatric speciation (isolation without geographic separation)
I can explain that speciation happens when gene flow stops and populations diverge until they can no longer interbreed
